/-
  TRAINING SPLIT of TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Atoms. Generated from Core/Vocab/Atoms.lean by
  ontology_provenance/nrs_tools/atoms_train.py: the definitions of the atoms whose only textual
  support is a test line are omitted. Do not edit; regenerate.
-/
/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Atoms
  The bijection with the atoms of ATOMS.md: exactly one definition per atom id, named `family_name`,
  each reading one field of `World` and nothing else. Attribute accessors of an atom carry the
  atom's name plus a suffix (`dev_traffic_signal_shows`, `ru_rider_posture_on_seat`).

  Rules of this file, held by the doctor:
  - every `\`family.name\`` in ATOMS.md has exactly one `def family_name` here and vice versa;
  - no thresholds, no comparisons against constants, no temporal lookback: a threshold is a rule's
    or a derived concept's business;
  - the `rel_*` atoms may compute geometry from kinematics, because their contract says they are
    "computed from kinematics; listed because a source may supply them measured" — a measured
    value, when the source gives one, is preferred; `rel_visible` reads a measured value only.

  Every atom is three-valued: `none` is "not observed on this source".
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.World
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Assumptions

namespace TrafficSpec

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Geometry helpers for the `rel_*` atoms (exact rationals; the one square root is an integer
-- square root at micrometre resolution).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
namespace Geom
def vsub (a b : Vec) : Vec := (Q.sub a.1 b.1, Q.sub a.2 b.2)
def vadd (a b : Vec) : Vec := (Q.add a.1 b.1, Q.add a.2 b.2)
def dot (a b : Vec) : Q := Q.add (Q.mul a.1 b.1) (Q.mul a.2 b.2)
/-- 2-D cross product `a × b`; positive when `b` is to the left of `a`. -/
def cross (a b : Vec) : Q := Q.sub (Q.mul a.1 b.2) (Q.mul a.2 b.1)
def normSq (a : Vec) : Q := dot a a
/-- Square root of a non-negative quantity in metres, floored to micrometres. -/
def sqrtMicro (q : Q) : Q :=
  if q.num ≤ 0 then Q.zero
  else
    let scaled : Int := (q.num * 1000000000000) / (q.den : Int)   -- µm²
    Units.micrometres (Int.ofNat (isqrt scaled.toNat))
def norm (a : Vec) : Q := sqrtMicro (normSq a)
/-- The unit vector along `a`; `none` for the zero vector only. `a` is first divided by its larger
    absolute component, so the vector normalised has length between 1 and √2 whatever `a`'s scale,
    and then by that length taken to micrometres (`norm`). The result is the exact unit vector times
    a factor of at least 1 and below 1 + 2·10⁻⁶, and is exact where the scaled length is a whole
    number of micrometres (every axis-aligned direction). -/
def unit (a : Vec) : Option Vec :=
  let m := Q.max (Q.abs a.1) (Q.abs a.2)
  if Q.isZero m then none
  else
    let b := (Q.div a.1 m, Q.div a.2 m)
    let n := norm b
    some (Q.div b.1 n, Q.div b.2 n)
/-- Components of `v` in the frame of heading `h` (longitudinal, lateral); lateral positive = left.
    `h` is read as a direction (`unit`), whatever its length; `v` keeps its own. -/
def inFrame (h v : Vec) : Option (Q × Q) := do
  let u ← unit h
  pure (dot u v, cross u v)
/-- Distance from a point to a segment. -/
def segmentDistance (p a b : Vec) : Q :=
  let ab := vsub b a
  let ap := vsub p a
  let l2 := normSq ab
  if Q.isZero l2 then norm ap
  else
    let t := Q.max Q.zero (Q.min (Q.ofInt 1) (Q.div (dot ap ab) l2))
    norm (vsub p (vadd a (Q.mul t ab.1, Q.mul t ab.2)))
/-- Whether a point lies inside a polygon (ray casting), for footprint-in-region tests. -/
def inPolygon (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
  let n := poly.length
  if n < 3 then false
  else
    let edges := (List.range n).map fun i => (poly[i]!, poly[(i + 1) % n]!)
    let crossings := edges.filter fun (a, b) =>
      let (ax, ay) := a; let (bx, by_) := b
      ((Q.le ay p.2) != (Q.le by_ p.2)) &&
        -- x-intersection of the edge with the horizontal line through p, compared with p.x
        (let dy := Q.sub by_ ay
         !Q.isZero dy &&
         Q.lt p.1 (Q.add ax (Q.div (Q.mul (Q.sub p.2 ay) (Q.sub bx ax)) dy)))
    crossings.length % 2 == 1
/-- The sign of `(b − a) × (c − a)`: 1 when `c` is to the left of `ab`, −1 to its right, 0 on its line. -/
def orient (a b c : Vec) : Int :=
  let k := (cross (vsub b a) (vsub c a)).num
  if k > 0 then 1 else if k < 0 then -1 else 0
/-- Whether `p` lies on the closed segment `ab`, given that it lies on its line. -/
def withinBox (p a b : Vec) : Bool :=
  Q.le (Q.min a.1 b.1) p.1 && Q.le p.1 (Q.max a.1 b.1) && Q.le (Q.min a.2 b.2) p.2 && Q.le p.2 (Q.max a.2 b.2)
/-- Whether the closed segments `ab` and `cd` share a point, touching and collinear overlap included. -/
def segmentsIntersect (a b c d : Vec) : Bool :=
  let o1 := orient a b c; let o2 := orient a b d; let o3 := orient c d a; let o4 := orient c d b
  (o1 * o2 < 0 && o3 * o4 < 0) || (o1 == 0 && withinBox c a b) || (o2 == 0 && withinBox d a b)
    || (o3 == 0 && withinBox a c d) || (o4 == 0 && withinBox b c d)
/-- The edges of a polygon, the last vertex closing to the first. -/
def edges (poly : List Vec) : List (Vec × Vec) :=
  let n := poly.length
  (List.range n).map fun i => (poly[i]!, poly[(i + 1) % n]!)
/-- Whether two polygons share a point as closed sets: an edge of one meets an edge of the other
    (touching counts), or one lies inside the other. Exact. -/
def polygonsOverlap (p q : List Vec) : Bool :=
  (edges p).any (fun (a, b) => (edges q).any fun (c, d) => segmentsIntersect a b c d)
    || p.any (inPolygon · q) || q.any (inPolygon · p)
/-- Distance from a point to a polygon's boundary: zero inside, the nearest edge outside. -/
def polygonDistance (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Option Q :=
  match poly with
  | [] => none
  | [a] => some (norm (vsub p a))
  | _ =>
    if inPolygon p poly then some Q.zero
    else
      let n := poly.length
      let ds := (List.range n).map fun i => segmentDistance p poly[i]! poly[(i + 1) % n]!
      ds.foldl (fun acc d => match acc with | none => some d | some a => some (Q.min a d)) none
/-- The point of a segment nearest a point. -/
def segmentNearest (p a b : Vec) : Vec :=
  let ab := vsub b a
  let l2 := normSq ab
  if Q.isZero l2 then a
  else
    let t := Q.max Q.zero (Q.min (Q.ofInt 1) (Q.div (dot (vsub p a) ab) l2))
    vadd a (Q.mul t ab.1, Q.mul t ab.2)
/-- The point of a polygon's boundary nearest a point. -/
def nearestPoint (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Option Vec :=
  match poly with
  | [] => none
  | [a] => some a
  | _ =>
    let n := poly.length
    let cs := (List.range n).map fun i => segmentNearest p poly[i]! poly[(i + 1) % n]!
    cs.foldl (fun acc c => match acc with
      | none => some c
      | some b => if Q.lt (normSq (vsub p c)) (normSq (vsub p b)) then some c else some b) none
/-- Every point of a polygon's boundary nearest a point: the nearest point of each edge whose
    distance is the least, so a tie keeps every equally near point whatever the vertex order. -/
def nearestPoints (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : List Vec :=
  match poly with
  | [] => []
  | [a] => [a]
  | _ =>
    let n := poly.length
    let cs := (List.range n).map fun i => segmentNearest p poly[i]! poly[(i + 1) % n]!
    match cs.map fun c => normSq (vsub p c) with
    | [] => []
    | d :: ds =>
      let m := ds.foldl Q.min d
      cs.filter fun c => Q.eq (normSq (vsub p c)) m
/-- The vector from the nearest point of polygon `p` to the nearest point of polygon `q`: zero when
    they share a point (`polygonsOverlap`), otherwise the shortest vector joining a vertex of one to
    the nearest point of the other's boundary, which for two convex polygons is the same for every
    nearest pair. `none` for an empty polygon. -/
def nearestOffset (p q : List Vec) : Option Vec :=
  if polygonsOverlap p q then some (Q.zero, Q.zero)
  else
    let fromP := p.filterMap fun c => (nearestPoint c q).map (vsub · c)
    let fromQ := q.filterMap fun c => (nearestPoint c p).map (vsub c ·)
    (fromP ++ fromQ).foldl (fun acc d => match acc with
      | none => some d
      | some e => if Q.lt (normSq d) (normSq e) then some d else some e) none
/-- The interval a polygon covers along the direction `u`, measured from `o`: (lowest, highest). -/
def span (u o : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Option (Q × Q) :=
  match poly.map fun c => dot u (vsub c o) with
  | [] => none
  | x :: xs => some (xs.foldl Q.min x, xs.foldl Q.max x)
/-- Twice the signed area of a polygon (the shoelace sum). -/
def area2 (poly : List Vec) : Q :=
  (edges poly).foldl (fun acc (a, b) => Q.add acc (cross a b)) Q.zero
/-- Whether a polygon's boundary crosses or touches itself: two edges that are not neighbours
    meet, or two neighbouring edges fold back along one line. -/
def selfIntersects (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
  let es := (edges poly).toArray
  let n := es.size
  (List.range n).any fun i => (List.range n).any fun j =>
    if j ≤ i then false
    else
      let (a, b) := es[i]!
      let (c, d) := es[j]!
      if j == i + 1 then orient a b d == 0 && Q.lt (dot (vsub b a) (vsub d c)) Q.zero
      else if i == 0 && j + 1 == n then orient c d b == 0 && Q.lt (dot (vsub d c) (vsub b a)) Q.zero
      else segmentsIntersect a b c d
/-- A simple polygon: at least three vertices, a non-zero area, and a boundary that neither crosses
    nor touches itself (a repeated vertex makes two edges that are not neighbours meet). -/
def simplePolygon (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
  poly.length ≥ 3 && !Q.isZero (area2 poly) && !selfIntersects poly
/-- Whether a point lies on a polygon's boundary. Exact. -/
def onBoundary (p : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
  (edges poly).any fun (a, b) => orient a b p == 0 && withinBox p a b
/-- The parameters `t` at which the line `p + t·u` meets the polygon's boundary: one per edge it
    crosses or touches, and both ends of an edge it runs along. `u` is not the zero vector. -/
def lineCrossings (p u : Vec) (poly : List Vec) : List Q :=
  (edges poly).flatMap fun (a, b) =>
    let d := vsub b a
    let w := vsub a p
    let den := cross u d
    if Q.isZero den then
      if Q.isZero (cross u w) then [Q.div (dot w u) (dot u u), Q.div (dot (vsub b p) u) (dot u u)] else []
    else
      let s := Q.div (cross w u) den
      if Q.le Q.zero s && Q.le s (Q.ofInt 1) then [Q.div (cross w d) den] else []
end Geom

-- Road structure and occupancy
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- Whether kind `a` refines kind `b`, reflexively and transitively. -/
def StructureKind.refines (a b : StructureKind) : Bool := a == b || a.ancestors.contains b

/-- Whether a source that cannot tell kind `m` (it is among `unobservedKinds`) leaves this structure's
    membership of `m`'s kinds open: always where `m` refines no kind other than an abstract one;
    otherwise only where the structure is labelled `m` or a kind `m` refines, since a structure of any
    other kind is known not to be one. -/
def Structure.maskApplies (st : Structure) (m : StructureKind) : Bool :=
  (m.parent?.filter (!·.isAbstract)).isNone || m.refines st.kind

/-- Whether a structure is of kind `k`: unknown where a kind the source cannot tell, applying to this
    structure, is `k` or a kind `k` refines (the label cannot be trusted for `k`); true where the
    structure's kind refines `k`; unknown where a kind the source cannot tell, applying to this
    structure, refines `k`; false otherwise. A parent never implies a kind refining it, two kinds
    refining one parent never imply each other, and a kind the source cannot tell never makes a known
    parent unknown. An abstract kind is the union of the kinds refining it: true where the structure
    is of one of them, unknown where it is of none and unknown for one, false otherwise. -/
def Structure.isOfKind (st : Structure) (k : StructureKind) : Option Bool :=
  let masked := st.unobservedKinds.filter st.maskApplies
  let concrete (k : StructureKind) : Option Bool :=
    if masked.any (k.refines ·) then none
    else if st.kind.refines k then some true
    else if masked.any (·.refines k) then none
    else some false
  if k.isAbstract then
    let vs := (StructureKind.all.filter (·.parent? == some k)).map concrete
    if vs.contains (some true) then some true else if vs.contains none then none else some false
  else concrete k

/-- Whether a region is of a kind (`Structure.isOfKind`); unknown for a region not in the scene. -/
def isKind (s : Scene) (r : RegionId) (k : StructureKind) : Option Bool :=
  (s.structure? r).bind (·.isOfKind k)

/-- Whether `r'` is lane `r`'s neighbour of the same direction on its left: decided false for every
    `r'` where `r` is first from the left, unknown where neither the neighbour nor the lane's place
    is observed. -/
def st_lane_left_of (s : Scene) (r r' : RegionId) : Option Bool :=
  match st_lane_adjacency_left s r with
  | some n => some (n == r')
  | none => if st_lane_adjacency_ordinal s r == some 1 then some false else none
/-- Whether `r'` is lane `r`'s neighbour of the same direction on its right: decided false for every
    `r'` where `r` is last of the lanes in its direction. -/

  match st_lane_adjacency_right s r with
  | some n => some (n == r')
  | none =>
    match st_lane_adjacency_ordinal s r, st_lane_adjacency_count s r with
    | some o, some n => if o == n then some false else none
    | _, _ => none

  | some d => some d

/-- Components of `b`'s position relative to `a` in `a`'s heading frame (longitudinal, lateral). -/
private def relFrame (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option (Q × Q) := do
  let pa ← kin_position s a
  let pb ← kin_position s b
  let ha ← kin_heading s a

    nearest point of `b`'s, each footprint read with its own heading and extent, given as its

    observed, and when a supplied gap has a negative component. -/
def rel_surface_gap (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option (Q × Q) :=

  | some g => if Q.isNonneg g.1 && Q.isNonneg g.2 then some g else none
  | none => do

    let fb ← footprint s b
    let d ← Geom.nearestOffset fa fb
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let (lon, lat) ← Geom.inFrame ha d
    pure (Q.abs lon, Q.abs lat)

def rel_surface_gap_lateral (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Q := (rel_surface_gap s a b).map (·.2)
/-- The distance between the nearest points of the two bodies, the gap's length: zero on contact
    or overlap, never negative. -/
def rel_surface_gap_distance (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Q := (rel_surface_gap s a b).map Geom.norm

/-- `a` and `b` share a lane and `a` is ahead of `b` along `a`'s heading. The lane is any region both
    occupy that is of kind lane (`Structure.isOfKind`): unknown when `a` is ahead and no shared region
    is known to be a lane but one may be. -/
def rel_ahead_behind_in_lane (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.aAheadOfB) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let ra ← rel_occupies_regions s a
    let rb ← rel_occupies_regions s b
    let (lon, _) ← relFrame s a b
    if !Q.lt lon Q.zero then some false
    else
      let shared := (s.structures.filter fun st => ra.contains st.id && rb.contains st.id).map (·.isOfKind .lane)
      if shared.contains (some true) then some true
      else if shared.contains none then none
      else some false
def rel_ahead_in_lane (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := rel_ahead_behind_in_lane s a b
def rel_behind_in_lane (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := rel_ahead_behind_in_lane s b a

/-- Signed overlap of the two footprints along `a`'s heading, each read with its own heading and
    extent: the length their projections on that axis share, positive when the bodies are side by
    side, otherwise the gap between the projections negated. A projection: it reads nothing across
    the axis, so a positive value is no contact and a negative one no distance between the bodies. -/
def rel_longitudinal_overlap (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Q :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.longitudinalOverlap) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let pa ← kin_position s a
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let u ← Geom.unit ha
    let fa ← footprint s a
    let fb ← footprint s b
    let (loA, hiA) ← Geom.span u pa fa
    let (loB, hiB) ← Geom.span u pa fb
    pure (Q.sub (Q.min hiA hiB) (Q.max loA loB))

/-- Headings opposed (cosine below `-cosTol`) and the distance decreasing. -/
def rel_oncoming (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) (cosTol : Q) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.oncoming) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let hb ← kin_heading s b
    let pa ← kin_position s a
    let pb ← kin_position s b
    let va ← kin_velocity s a
    let vb ← kin_velocity s b
    let ua ← Geom.unit ha
    let ub ← Geom.unit hb
    let closing := Q.lt (Geom.dot (Geom.vsub pb pa) (Geom.vsub vb va)) Q.zero
    pure (Q.lt (Geom.dot ua ub) (Q.neg cosTol) && closing)

/-- Headings aligned (cosine above `cosTol`). -/
def rel_same_direction (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) (cosTol : Q) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.sameDirection) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let hb ← kin_heading s b
    let ua ← Geom.unit ha
    let ub ← Geom.unit hb
    pure (Q.gt (Geom.dot ua ub) cosTol)

/-- `b` relative to `a` in `a`'s frame: (longitudinal, lateral), lateral positive to the left. -/
def rel_bearing (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Vec :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.bearing) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => relFrame s a b
def rel_bearing_right (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.lt v.2 Q.zero
def rel_bearing_left (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.gt v.2 Q.zero
def rel_bearing_ahead (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.gt v.1 Q.zero
def rel_bearing_behind (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.lt v.1 Q.zero

/-- The bodies touch or overlap. -/
def rel_contact (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.contact) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => (rel_surface_gap s a b).map fun g => Q.le g.1 Q.zero && Q.le g.2 Q.zero

/-- `b` is in `a`'s line of sight, as the source tested it; never computed. -/
def rel_visible (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (s.relation a b).bind (·.visible)

end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule
3	  What a specification is: binders with class formulas, an applicability and an obligation, and
4	  the declarations a reviewer needs (parameters, assumptions, declared intentions,
5	  operationalizations, residues, narrowings, the rules it composes, the surrogate flag).
6	
7	  A residue is a span of the text the rule does not capture at all; the plan declares it and the
8	  rule repeats it verbatim. A narrowing is a reading the coder chose on a span the plan does
9	  carry, stated here so the review judges the rule as it is: the span it names and why. The
10	  coder may add narrowings and never residues.
11	
12	  Applicability and obligation are two formulas because a rule whose situation never arises is
13	  not compliant, it is not engaged: `notApplicable` is a verdict of its own, the witness check can
14	  demand a scenario for it, and a monitor reads the applicability as the trigger and the
15	  obligation as what to verify once triggered.
16	
17	  A surrogate rule (the whole duty is an operationalized standard) is monitored like any other,
18	  but its verdicts are evidence about the standard, never the law's own verdict; the flag is what
19	  the monitor and the export propagate so the two are never summed.
20	
21	  This file holds the declarations only and imports no evaluator: a rule file that imports it
22	  can state a rule but cannot read a scene, evaluate a formula or build evidence. Evaluation and
23	  the static check are in RuleEval.lean, which nothing under Rules/ may import.

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule
  What a specification is: binders with class formulas, an applicability and an obligation, and
  the declarations a reviewer needs (parameters, assumptions, declared intentions,
  operationalizations, residues, narrowings, the rules it composes, the surrogate flag).

  A residue is a span of the text the rule does not capture at all; the plan declares it and the
  rule repeats it verbatim. A narrowing is a reading the coder chose on a span the plan does
  carry, stated here so the review judges the rule as it is: the span it names and why. The
  coder may add narrowings and never residues.

  Applicability and obligation are two formulas because a rule whose situation never arises is
  not compliant, it is not engaged: `notApplicable` is a verdict of its own, the witness check can
  demand a scenario for it, and a monitor reads the applicability as the trigger and the
  obligation as what to verify once triggered.

  A surrogate rule (the whole duty is an operationalized standard) is monitored like any other,
  but its verdicts are evidence about the standard, never the law's own verdict; the flag is what
  the monitor and the export propagate so the two are never summed.

  This file holds the declarations only and imports no evaluator: a rule file that imports it
  can state a rule but cannot read a scene, evaluate a formula or build evidence. Evaluation and
  the static check are in RuleEval.lean, which nothing under Rules/ may import.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Formula
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Unknown

namespace TrafficSpec

/-- A binder: a variable and the class formula (over `ru_*` atoms and class-level derived
    concepts) a track must satisfy to be bound to it. The subject comes first. -/
structure Binder where
  name : String
  cls : Formula
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

/-- A reading chosen on a span the record carries, declared where it is made: the span (a
    segmentation id for a rule, a run of the contract's words for a concept) and what the formulas
    state more narrowly than the words. `kind` is `reading` where the words leave the choice open,
    `observable_reading` where a word with no observable counterpart is read through the conduct
    or the feature it refers to, `no_atom` or `no_operator` where the vocabulary or the language
    cannot state the words — a declaration the gate returns for a gap, never a reading the rule
    stands on. -/
structure Narrowing where
  span : String
  why : String
  kind : String := "reading"
  deriving Repr, Inhabited, DecidableEq

structure Rule where
  id : String                                   -- the node id, derived from the law id
  laws : List String                            -- the corpus ids this rule formalizes
  binders : List Binder
  applicability : Formula
  obligation : Formula
  assumptions : List AsmId := []
  intentions : List IntId := []                 -- the declared intentions its formulas read
  operationalizations : List Operationalization := []
  residues : List String := []                  -- what the text says and the rule does not capture
  narrowings : List Narrowing := []             -- readings the coder chose on carried spans
  surrogate : Bool := false
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

inductive Verdict
  | violated
  | compliant
  | notApplicable
  | unknown (why : List UnknownReason)
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

namespace Verdict
def tag : Verdict → String
  | .violated => "violated"
  | .compliant => "compliant"
  | .notApplicable => "not_applicable"
  | .unknown _ => "unknown"
def reasons : Verdict → List UnknownReason
  | .unknown w => w
  | _ => []
instance : ToString Verdict := ⟨tag⟩
end Verdict

/-- Kleene combination of the two formulas: not engaged ↦ notApplicable, engaged and the
    obligation decided ↦ compliant/violated, anything undecided ↦ unknown with its reasons. -/
def verdictAt (app obl : R) : Verdict :=
  match app.v with
  | .f => .notApplicable
  | .u => .unknown app.why
  | .t =>
    match obl.v with
    | .t => .compliant
    | .f => .violated
    | .u => .unknown obl.why

theorem verdictAt_notApplicable (app obl : R) (h : app.v = .f) : verdictAt app obl = .notApplicable := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [h]
theorem verdictAt_violated (app obl : R) (ha : app.v = .t) (ho : obl.v = .f) : verdictAt app obl = .violated := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [ha, ho]
theorem verdictAt_compliant (app obl : R) (ha : app.v = .t) (ho : obl.v = .t) : verdictAt app obl = .compliant := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [ha, ho]

namespace Rule
/-- The formulas a rule consists of, class formulas first. -/
def formulas (r : Rule) : List Formula := r.binders.map (·.cls) ++ [r.applicability, r.obligation]
/-- Atom, primitive and concept names the rule reads. -/
def atoms (r : Rule) : List String := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.atoms).eraseDups
/-- Reading parameters the rule names. -/
def params (r : Rule) : List ParamName := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.params).eraseDups
/-- Rules the rule composes. -/
def composes (r : Rule) : List String := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.composed).eraseDups
/-- Assumptions the formulas read. -/
def usedAssumptions (r : Rule) : List AsmId := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.assumptions).eraseDups
/-- Declared intentions the formulas read. -/
def usedIntentions (r : Rule) : List IntId := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.intentions).eraseDups
def binderNames (r : Rule) : List String := r.binders.map (·.name)
def subject (r : Rule) : Option String := r.binders.head?.map (·.name)

/-- The rule and, transitively, the rules it composes (each once). -/
def closure (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : List Rule :=
  let rec go (fuel : Nat) (seen : List String) (todo : List Rule) : List Rule :=
    match fuel, todo with
    | 0, _ | _, [] => []
    | fuel + 1, x :: rest =>
      let next := x.composes.filterMap fun id =>
        if seen.contains id then none else rules.find? (·.id == id)
      x :: go fuel (seen ++ next.map (·.id)) (rest ++ next)
  go (rules.length + 1) [r.id] [r]

/-- Whether the rule reads a declared intention, in its own formulas or through a rule it
    composes at any depth. -/
def readsIntention (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : Bool :=
  (closure rules r).any fun x => !x.usedIntentions.isEmpty
end Rule

end TrafficSpec

  operationalization and composition below is written, and every choice the text did not dictate).

    s1 (subject): The driver of a vehicle
    sib1 (sibling): shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or yield in compliance with a yield sign, in compliance with the manner prescribed in subsection 1 [NRS-484B-257-1], prior to entering an intersection
    c1 (condition): if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto
    c2 (condition): although not a part of a through highway
    st1 (standard): and shall proceed cautiously,
    ob1 (obligation): yielding to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield and which are within the intersection
    st2 (standard): or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
    c3 (condition): during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule

namespace TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B_257_2_o2

/-- The binders, as arguments (order and names are the node's). -/
def vV : Arg := .var "v"

def pCautiousProceedMaxSpeed : Term := .param "p.cautious_proceed_max_speed"
def pStandstillSpeedTolerance : Term := .param "p.standstill_speed_tolerance"
def pYieldConflictHorizon : Term := .param "p.yield_conflict_horizon"
def pYieldHeadwayTime : Term := .param "p.yield_headway_time"
def pYieldMinClearance : Term := .param "p.yield_min_clearance"

def zeroMetres : Term := .lit Q.zero .metre

  .existsRegion (.lit "travel_region") "c"
    (.and (.atom "st_lane_enters" [.var "c", .var "j"] [])
      (.or (.existsDevice (.lit "stop_sign") "ds"
              (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "ds", .var "c"] []))
           (.existsDevice (.lit "yield_sign") "dy"
              (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "dy", .var "c"] []))))

    the junction itself or on the subject's own approach carrier. -/

  .existsUser "w"
    (.and (.atom "ru_aggregate" [.var "w", .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic"] [])
      (.and (.atom "rel_occupies" [.var "w", .var "j"] [])
        (.existsRegion (.lit "travel_region") "cc"
          (.and (.or (.same (.var "cc") (.var "j"))
                     (.and (.atom "st_lane_enters" [.var "cc", .var "j"] [])
                           (.atom "rel_occupies" [vV, .var "cc"] [])))
            (.or (.existsDevice (.lit "human_direction") "o"
                    (.and (.atom "dev_human_direction_role" [.var "o", .lit "police_officer"] [])
                          (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "o", .var "cc"] [])))

                    (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "g", .var "cc"] [])))))))

    c1 (condition): if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto
    c2 (condition): although not a part of a through highway
    st1 (standard): and shall proceed cautiously,
    ob1 (obligation): yielding to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield and which are within the intersection
    st2 (standard): or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
    c3 (condition): during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

  Elements (span → atoms, derived):
    e1: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic', 'dev.human_direction', 'dev.traffic_signal', 'dev.governs', 'rel.occupies', 'st.travel_region', 'st.lane_enters', 'st.intersection'], derived []
    s1: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle'], derived []
    c1: atoms ['dev.stop_sign', 'dev.yield_sign', 'dev.governs', 'st.travel_region', 'st.lane_enters', 'st.intersection', 'rel.occupies'], derived []
    ob1: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle', 'dev.stop_sign', 'dev.yield_sign', 'dev.governs', 'rel.occupies', 'st.travel_region', 'st.lane_enters', 'st.intersection', 'rel.surface_gap', 'rel.contact', 'kin.speed', 'prim.closest_approach_within', 'prim.closest_approach_distance'], derived []
    c3: atoms ['rel.occupies', 'st.intersection', 'kin.speed'], derived []

  How each span is written

  s1 — `clsV`: the binder's class is the single admitted aggregate, `ru_aggregate v
  "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"`. The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, as the
  record's observable reading says; nothing is restated here.

  c1 — `signErectedAtAnEntrance`: a travel region `c` other than the junction itself whose entrance
  end is the junction `j` (`st_lane_enters c j`) that a stop sign or a yield sign governs
  (`dev_governs` under a quantifier over devices of kind `stop_sign` / `yield_sign`). "One or more
  entrances thereto" is the existential: any entrance of that junction, not only the subject's own.
  The sign's presence on the road is its erection (the record's observable reading). That the
  junction is not among its own entrances is the `st.lane_enters` contract's own content — a carrier
  runs into the intersection at its entrance end, and no junction is an approach to itself — not a
  reading chosen here.

  c3 — the junction region of kind `intersection` the subject's footprint overlaps
  (`rel_occupies v j`), with its speed above `p.standstill_speed_tolerance` for "is moving across or
  within". Both are read again in the obligation's guard, so that the duty speaks of the same
  junction and only while the subject is moving in it (Core evaluates the two formulas separately).

  e1 — `trafficControlled`: a road user `w` of the aggregate `DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic` whose
  footprint overlaps that junction, where a travel region `cc` that is the junction itself
  (`same cc j`) or an approach carrier of it the subject occupies
  (`st_lane_enters cc j` and `rel_occupies v cc`) is governed by a device of kind `human_direction`
  with role `police_officer`, or by a device of kind `traffic_signal`. Both limbs of the record's
  reading ("the junction the subject is at or on its own approach carrier") are carried; the
  exception is negated into the applicability as a whole.

  observation at which the guard holds.

  subject that is of the aggregate `DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle` and is not itself obligated
  (`notObligated`: some approach carrier of that junction it occupies that no stop sign and no yield
  sign governs), and which either lies within the junction (`rel_occupies u j`) or is an immediate
  hazard (`immediateHazard`), the subject must not come into contact with it (`rel_contact`) and
  must not breach the clearance while the two draw together (`clearanceBreached`): where their
  centres approach each other under constant velocities within `p.yield_conflict_horizon`

  (`prim_closest_approach_distance`) nor the present distance between the nearest points of the two
  bodies (`rel_surface_gap`) may fall below `p.yield_min_clearance` — the three atoms ob1's
  justification names for "yielding", read together. `immediateHazard` is st2's gap-acceptance
  convention: the vehicle's ground distance to the junction (`st_region_geometry_distance`) at most
  its own speed times `p.yield_headway_time`, or the conflict figure (`conflictPredicted`, the
  centres' closest approach below the clearance).

  the centre figure the primitive gives and the nearest-point figure `rel.surface_gap` gives, read
  while the two draw together), st2's two figures read as alternatives, the duty read at every
  junction the selection picks, and the protected vehicle's approach carrier read as a travel region
  other than the junction itself.

import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule

namespace TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B_257_2_o2

/-- The binders, as arguments (order and names are the node's). -/
def vV : Arg := .var "v"

/-- The reading's parameters; no value of any of them lives in this file. -/
def pCautiousProceedMaxSpeed : Term := .param "p.cautious_proceed_max_speed"
def pStandstillSpeedTolerance : Term := .param "p.standstill_speed_tolerance"
def pYieldConflictHorizon : Term := .param "p.yield_conflict_horizon"
def pYieldHeadwayTime : Term := .param "p.yield_headway_time"
def pYieldMinClearance : Term := .param "p.yield_min_clearance"

def zeroMetres : Term := .lit Q.zero .metre

/-- Class of `v`: ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle -/
def clsV : Formula := .atom "ru_aggregate" [vV, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"] []

/-- c3: the subject's footprint overlaps the junction `j`. -/
def atJunction : Formula := .atom "rel_occupies" [vV, .var "j"] []

/-- c3: the subject is moving. -/
def moving : Formula := .cmp (.measure "kin_speed" [vV]) .gt pStandstillSpeedTolerance

/-- c1: a stop sign or a yield sign governs a travel region, other than the junction itself, whose
    entrance end is `j`. -/
def signErectedAtAnEntrance : Formula :=
  .existsRegion (.lit "travel_region") "c"
    (.and (.not (.same (.var "c") (.var "j")))
      (.and (.atom "st_lane_enters" [.var "c", .var "j"] [])
        (.or (.existsDevice (.lit "stop_sign") "ds"
                (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "ds", .var "c"] []))
             (.existsDevice (.lit "yield_sign") "dy"
                (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "dy", .var "c"] [])))))

/-- e1: traffic at `j` is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal, read on
    the junction itself or on the subject's own approach carrier. -/
def trafficControlled : Formula :=
  .existsUser "w"
    (.and (.atom "ru_aggregate" [.var "w", .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic"] [])
      (.and (.atom "rel_occupies" [.var "w", .var "j"] [])
        (.existsRegion (.lit "travel_region") "cc"
          (.and (.or (.same (.var "cc") (.var "j"))
                     (.and (.atom "st_lane_enters" [.var "cc", .var "j"] [])
                           (.atom "rel_occupies" [vV, .var "cc"] [])))
            (.or (.existsDevice (.lit "human_direction") "o"
                    (.and (.atom "dev_human_direction_role" [.var "o", .lit "police_officer"] [])
                          (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "o", .var "cc"] [])))
                 (.existsDevice (.lit "traffic_signal") "g"
                    (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "g", .var "cc"] [])))))))

/-- Applicability: e1 (exception): Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:; c1 (condition): if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto; c2 (condition): although not a part of a through highway; c3 (condition): during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection. -/
def applicability : Formula :=
  .existsRegion (.lit "intersection") "j"
    (.and atJunction
      (.and moving
        (.and signErectedAtAnEntrance
          (.not trafficControlled))))

/-- st1: proceeding cautiously. -/
def cautiously : Formula := .cmp (.measure "kin_speed" [vV]) .le pCautiousProceedMaxSpeed

/-- The subject and `u` draw together within the horizon (their centres approach each other under
    constant velocities). -/
def drawingTogether : Formula :=
  .derived "prim_closest_approach_within" [vV, .var "u"] [pYieldConflictHorizon]

/-- The centre distance at that closest approach is below the clearance. -/
def centresBelowClearance : Formula :=
  .cmp (.quantity "prim_closest_approach_distance" [vV, .var "u"] [pYieldConflictHorizon])
       .lt pYieldMinClearance

/-- st2: the conflict figure of the hazard convention — the closest approach of the two centres
    within the horizon below the clearance. -/
def conflictPredicted : Formula := .and drawingTogether centresBelowClearance

/-- ob1: the clearance the subject must keep while the two draw together — neither the closest
    approach of their centres nor the present distance between the nearest points of their bodies
    may fall below the clearance. -/
def clearanceBreached : Formula :=
  .and drawingTogether
    (.or centresBelowClearance
         (.cmp (.measure "rel_surface_gap" [vV, .var "u"]) .lt pYieldMinClearance))

/-- ob1: `u` reached `j` through an approach carrier of it that no stop sign and no yield sign
    governs. -/
def notObligated : Formula :=
  .existsRegion (.lit "travel_region") "cu"
    (.and (.not (.same (.var "cu") (.var "j")))
      (.and (.atom "rel_occupies" [.var "u", .var "cu"] [])
        (.and (.atom "st_lane_enters" [.var "cu", .var "j"] [])
          (.and (.not (.existsDevice (.lit "stop_sign") "dus"
                        (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "dus", .var "cu"] [])))
                (.not (.existsDevice (.lit "yield_sign") "duy"
                        (.atom "dev_governs" [.var "duy", .var "cu"] [])))))))

/-- st2: `u` approaches so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard. -/
def immediateHazard : Formula :=
  .or (.cmp (.measure "st_region_geometry_distance" [.var "u", .var "j"]) .le
            (.mul (.measure "kin_speed" [.var "u"]) pYieldHeadwayTime))
      conflictPredicted

/-- ob1 with st2: the vehicles this duty protects. -/
def owedPrecedence : Formula :=
  .and (.not (.same (.var "u") vV))
    (.and (.atom "ru_aggregate" [.var "u", .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"] [])
      (.and notObligated
        (.or (.atom "rel_occupies" [.var "u", .var "j"] [])
             immediateHazard)))

/-- ob1: granting precedence to `u`. -/
def grantsPrecedence : Formula :=
  .and (.not (.atom "rel_contact" [vV, .var "u"] []))
       (.not clearanceBreached)

/-- Obligation: st1 (standard): and shall proceed cautiously,; ob1 (obligation): yielding to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield and which are within the intersection; st2 (standard): or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard -/
def obligation : Formula :=
  .forallRegion (.lit "intersection") "j"
    (.implies (.and atJunction (.and moving signErectedAtAnEntrance))
      (.and cautiously
        (.forallUser "u" (.implies owedPrecedence grantsPrecedence))))

def rule : Rule :=
  { id := "NRS_484B_257_2_o2"
    laws := ["NRS-484B-257-2"]
    binders :=
      [ { name := "v", cls := clsV } ]
    applicability := applicability
    obligation := obligation
    assumptions := []
    intentions := []
    operationalizations :=
      [ { standard := "and shall proceed cautiously"
          concepts := ["kin.speed", "prim.closest_approach_distance", "prim.closest_approach_within", "rel.occupies", "st.intersection"]
          params := ["p.cautious_proceed_max_speed", "p.yield_conflict_horizon", "p.yield_min_clearance"]
          convention := "A low-speed stopping-distance convention bounds the caution: crossing the junction after obeying the sign, the subject's speed stays at or below p.cautious_proceed_max_speed, the speed at which a vehicle can be brought to rest within the junction's conflict area on seeing a road user it must give way to. The degree of the hazard enters through the conflict-avoidance convention, the closest approach under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon staying clear of p.yield_min_clearance, so that the bound moves with the proximity and closing speed of the road users the same sentence names rather than switching on their presence alone."
          surrogate := false }
      , { standard := "or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard"
          concepts := ["kin.speed", "prim.closest_approach_distance", "prim.closest_approach_within", "rel.occupies", "rel.surface_gap", "st.intersection", "st.lane_enters", "st.region_geometry", "st.travel_region"]
          params := ["p.yield_headway_time", "p.yield_conflict_horizon", "p.yield_min_clearance"]
          convention := "Gap-acceptance convention for a crossing from a sign-controlled entrance. 'So closely' is the other vehicle's distance to the junction, which st.region_geometry gives as 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', read on a vehicle on a carrier entering that junction (rel.occupies, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters): the vehicle is so close where that distance is at most its own speed (kin.speed) times p.yield_headway_time, so the bound moves with its speed -- a faster approach makes a greater distance count, a slower one a smaller. The immediacy is read in the same breath by the conflict-avoidance convention: the closest approach between the two bodies under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon falling below p.yield_min_clearance, measured between the nearest points of the bodies by rel.surface_gap. Both figures are the reading's, from gap-acceptance tables for a crossing manoeuvre."
          surrogate := false } ]
    residues := ["'although not a part of a through highway' adds no observable condition: it is concessive, saying that the cautious proceeding and the yielding are owed even where the junction is not part of a through highway, so the duty is the same whether or not it is. Reading it as a condition would make the rule apply only at junctions off a through highway, which is narrower than the words."]  -- the node's, verbatim; not yours to change
    narrowings :=
      [ { span := "ob1"
          why := "The clearance the duty keeps is read with both measures the span's justification names, because no primitive gives the closest approach between the nearest points of two bodies: where the two draw together within p.yield_conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within), the duty is breached when the centre distance at that closest approach (prim.closest_approach_distance) is below p.yield_min_clearance, and also when the present distance between the nearest points of the bodies (rel.surface_gap) is below it, which catches two long bodies passing closer than the clearance while their centres stay further apart. Where the two do not draw together at all, neither figure is read: a road user moving away is granted precedence."
          kind := "reading" }
      , { span := "ob1"
          why := "The duty is read at every intersection the applicability's selection picks: the obligation quantifies universally over regions of kind st.intersection and rewrites that whole selection (the subject's footprint overlapping the junction, its moving, and a stop or yield sign at one of the junction's entrances) as the guard of the implication, since a region bound in the applicability is not in scope in the obligation."
          kind := "reading" }
      , { span := "ob1"
          why := "The approach carrier through which a protected vehicle reached the junction is read as a travel region other than the junction itself: a junction is no approach to itself, and st.lane_enters is not recorded on it, so reading the junction as its own entrance would leave the vehicle's obligation unknown wherever it stands in the junction."
          kind := "reading" }

/-
  Witnesses for NRS_484B_257_2_o2.

  The geometry (every figure here is the witness's own and appears nowhere in the rule):

  A plus-shaped junction, region 10, a 16 m square from (-8, -8) to (8, 8). Three approach
  carriers run into it, each recorded as entering region 10:
    - region 11, the subject's lane: northbound, x in [0, 4], y in [-60, -8];
    - region 14, the second northbound lane of the same leg: x in [4, 8], y in [-60, -8];
    - region 12, the crossing street's westbound lane: x in [8, 88], y in [0, 4].
  The subject (track 1) is a 4 m by 2 m car heading north; the other vehicle (track 2) is a van
  heading west on region 12 or north on region 14. Signs govern carriers, never the junction:
  device 20 is a stop sign on 11, device 21 a yield sign on 11, device 22 a stop sign on 12,
  device 25 a yield sign on 12; device 23 is a traffic signal governing 11 and device 24 a police
  officer directing the junction itself.

  Each trace is three observations one second apart with the scene held still, so that every
  instant carries the same verdict; the rule looks back over no window, so no scenario names one.
  Occupancy is read from the polygons where a body's reference point settles it, and stated where a
  body straddles two regions (a van partly in the junction and partly on its own carrier).

import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_257_2_o2
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_257_2_o2

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n
def mps (n : Int) : Q := Units.metresPerSecond n

-- Binders ↦ tracks: v ↦ 1

/-- The junction: a 16 m square. -/
def junction : Structure := Build.rect 10 .intersection (m (-8)) (m (-8)) (m 8) (m 8)

/-- The subject's approach carrier: the right-hand northbound lane of the south leg. -/
def southLane : Structure :=
  Build.lane 11 [(m 0, m (-60)), (m 4, m (-60)), (m 4, m (-8)), (m 0, m (-8))]
    Build.north (enters := some 10)

/-- The second northbound lane of the south leg. -/
def southLane2 : Structure :=
  Build.lane 14 [(m 4, m (-60)), (m 8, m (-60)), (m 8, m (-8)), (m 4, m (-8))]
    Build.north (enters := some 10)

/-- The crossing street's westbound approach carrier. -/
def eastLane : Structure :=
  Build.lane 12 [(m 8, m 0), (m 88, m 0), (m 88, m 4), (m 8, m 4)]
    Build.west (enters := some 10)

def roads : List Structure := [junction, southLane, southLane2, eastLane]

def stopForSubject : Device := Build.sign 20 .stopSign [11]
def yieldForSubject : Device := Build.sign 21 .yieldSign [11]
def stopForCross : Device := Build.sign 22 .stopSign [12]
def yieldForCross : Device := Build.sign 25 .yieldSign [12]
def signalForSubject : Device := Build.signal 23 [11] [.circularGreen]
def officerAtJunction : Device :=
  { Build.device 24 .humanDirection [10] with
      humanRole := some .policeOfficer
      humanIndication := some .proceed }

/-- The subject: a 4 m by 2 m car heading north at `speed`. -/
def car (pos : Vec) (speed : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user 1 [.motorVehicle] pos Build.north speed (m 2, m 1, cm 75)

/-- A van of the crossing street, heading west, `2 · halfLen` long. -/
def vanWest (pos : Vec) (speed : Q) (halfLen : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user 2 [.motorVehicle] pos Build.west speed (halfLen, m 1, m 1)

/-- A van on the south leg's second lane, heading north, 5 m long. -/
def vanNorth (pos : Vec) (speed : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user 2 [.motorVehicle] pos Build.north speed (cm 250, m 1, m 1)

/-- The subject in the junction and a van straddling the junction and its own carrier. -/
def straddleOccupancy : List (TrackId × RegionId) := [(1, 10), (2, 10), (2, 12)]

/-- `forbid` (violated): A stop sign governs the car's entrance to a junction where the crossing street's entrances carry no sign. The car halts, then pulls across the junction at 9 m/s while a van whose entrance carries no sign is within the junction, and the two bodies touch. -/
